newsitem.title: USA: West African, Colombian crudes roaming US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: West African, Colombian crudes roaming US Gulf.

text.p: Sweet West African and Colombian crudes were roaming the U.S. Gulf in search of buyers on Wednesday, highlighting the crude market's continued oversupply, traders said.
Sour crudes were seen weakening as a result of the U.N. Security Council's renewal of the Iraqi oil-for-food deal for another six months, traders said.

Several June cargoes of Nigerian crude were still looking for homes. A U.S. equity producer was offering a VLCC of Qua Iboe arriving end-June, asking in the neighborhood of 40 cents a barrel over dated Brent, traders said.
The West African market was shaken on Tuesday by the sale of a Nigerian Brass River cargo for June 22-24 loading at dated Brent plus 33 cents, about 20 cents less than the last reported deal.

From Colombia, a European equity producer sold a cargo of Cusiana to a U.S. refiner for a discount of $1.42 a barrel to West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, down seven cents from the last confirmed deal, trade sources said.
The 550,000 barrel cargo loads June 30 to July 1.
Robust Caribbean freight rates pushed down the latest price, even though a tight transatlantic arbitrage has restricted supplies of competing Brent cargoes in the U.S. Gulf.
The transatlantic arbitrage between July WTI and dated Brent was around $1.80-85 Wednesday afternoon. Coupled with high freight rates, traders said the arb was unworkable.
Meanwhile, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol is seeking bids for two Cusiana cargoes loading July 6-10 and July 15-19, traders said.
Among other Colombian grades, a U.S. company was offering a Cano Limon loading in mid-July, asking $2.50 a barrel under WTI/Cushing.
A trading house was offering a Vasconia cargo loading July 12-16, asking $3.40 a barrel under the U.S. benchmark.
Separately, traders said a distressed Saharan Blend cargo had been sold into the U.S., but the deal could not be confirmed.
